data.title: Database Write
data.tagline: Writing new or updated data to a database and committing the change
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish a success message from a completed database write and verify both the record and the refresh read.
data.description: After a user changes a nickname, the backend must complete and confirm the database write so refresh can read it back. A successful response alone does not prove that, and a write is not the same as backup, replication, or immediate visibility everywhere.

learning.assumes: You have used a page that saves data and reads it again after refresh.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish a success message from a completed database write and verify both the record and the refresh read.

distinctions.label: Transaction
distinctions.explanation: Database Write focuses on single data persistence and commits; a Transaction groups multiple writes into an indivisible commit or rollback boundary.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: A page showing save success early does not prove the database write completed; after checking input and permission, write the target record and wait for commit before returning the actual result.

explanation.title: How to observe the improvement
explanation.text: Return success only after the write completes, or return the specific failure instead of relying on early local state. After refresh, query with the same id and show the saved nickname.

explanation.title: Publishing grades also requires a confirmed write
explanation.text: After a teacher publishes a grade, the grade record must be written and committed. Reopening the student's grade page and reading the new score confirms the write completed.

data.boundary: Writing to a database is not the same as backing up, replicating to every node, or making every read immediately see the value.

lessonPractice.title: The API returns 200, but refreshing the page still shows the old nickname. What evidence should you check first?

options.label: Verify the write and commit completed, then check whether refresh reads the same record
options.feedback: Correct. The database record proves whether the write happened, and the refresh target proves the page requested that same data.

options.label: Only update the local nickname after clicking save so the page looks correct first
options.feedback: That changes only the current page; refresh still depends on a real write and proves nothing about the database.

options.label: Delay the success response for a few seconds and see whether refresh sometimes changes
options.feedback: A delay proves neither that writing finished nor whether the read used the wrong record or an uncommitted value.

data.agentPrompt: The API returns 200 but the old nickname returns after refresh. Trace validation, the database write, commit completion, and response timing, and confirm refresh reads the same record. Fix it, save once, refresh once, and inspect both the database row and API response; do not only change local state.
